problem: Existing generative world models (video / novel-view synthesis) predict pixels rather than maintaining an explicit, updatable, semantic 3D belief over unobserved space, so they lack 3D memory, multi-hypothesis uncertainty, sequential updating and semantic prediction for embodied agents.
motivation: Agents in unfamiliar environments must form beliefs over both seen and unseen regions and revise them as observations arrive. Pixel-space rollouts drift geometrically and cannot be queried semantically, and imagine-then-lift pipelines are decoupled and inconsistent over long horizons.
key_idea: Cast world modeling as POMDP belief inference in 3D: a scene-level diffusion model predicts and autoregressively updates explicit semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from streaming egocentric RGB, sampling multiple hypotheses for planning.
insight: Explicit 3D structure gives cross-view consistency (better 2D metrics and object permanence than DFoT/NWM/GEN3C) and enables planning by rendering semantic maps along imagined paths. Ablation on simulated ObjNav: removing geometry drops SR 45.83→17.50 and a single hypothesis drops it to 35.14, so both geometric grounding and multi-hypothesis sampling matter. Imagine-then-lift baselines (DFoT-VGGT, NWM-VGGT) perform near reconstruction-only VGGT, so a joint 3D generative model is what helps.
method: Belief formulation: belief b(s_t)=P(s_t|o_1:t) represented as 3DGS z=z_o ∪ z_i (observed + imagined Gaussians with mean, covariance, opacity, SH, semantic embedding); autoregressive update z^{t+1}~p(z^{t+1}|o^{t+1},z_o^t), where imagined Gaussians are replaced each step and per-step cost is constant

Architecture: shared U-ViT backbone (from DFoT) with an MVSplat-style multi-view Transformer + cost-volume depth predictor producing Gaussians, and a lightweight semantic head projecting features to per-pixel CLIP-aligned maps

Scene-level 3D diffusion: following DFM, diffusion is applied to the target view; the network predicts a 3DGS scene from context and noisy target, renders it to a clean-view estimate, and iterates the reverse process

Training objective: RGB (L1+LPIPS) loss on target and context views, CLIP/OpenCLIP+DINOv3 patch distillation semantic loss, optional masked L1 depth loss, depth smoothness, feature alignment and VGGT feature alignment

Belief-guided planning: frontier/observed-goal waypoint sampling, A* candidate paths, render imagined views along paths from 3 sampled beliefs, score via open-vocabulary semantic queries (goal progress and information gain), execute a short prefix and replan
3D-CORE benchmark: AI2-THOR/ProcTHOR/Objaverse tasks for Object Completion (233), Room Completion (263) and Object Permanence (474), with DFoT-VGGT as the imagine-then-lift baseline

setting.backbone: 3D-Belief: U-ViT (DFoT init) + MVSplat depth predictor, trained with diffusion; planning uses learned semantic head, no VLM
setting.training_data: Mix of SPOC (AI2-THOR), RealEstate10K, DL3DV, HM3D with equal-weight sampling; 250K steps, batch 1, single H100; separate model trained on RealEstate10K for real-world
setting.observation: egocentric RGB with camera poses (real robot: RGB plus wheel odometry; depth only used for scale alignment)
setting.action_space: waypoint/path planning via A* on frontier waypoints, executed as low-level navigation actions
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (ProcTHOR houses, SPOC protocol); real world Hello Robot Stretch 3
setting.privileged: none (poses given; real-world uses sensed depth for per-sequence metric scale alignment of predicted depth)

numbers.eval_set_note: 135 unseen houses; reported over 120 episodes per CI stats
numbers.extra: trained on SPOC/RE10K/DL3DV/HM3D; no VLM tokens
numbers.evidence: Table 1 Object navigation results in simulations and the real world

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 target objects, 3 start locations, mock apartment

numbers_note: Sim/real ObjNav are custom SPOC-style AI2-THOR benchmarks and a custom real setup, not canonical benchmarks. Also reports 2D quality (AI2-THOR PSNR 28.81, SSIM 0.928, LPIPS 0.0502, FID 47.24, FVD 271.8; RE10K PSNR 24.878, FVD 50.993), 3D-CORE, and SAT-Real 88.7 avg, not listed as navigation numbers.
results: 3D-Belief reaches 59.17 SR in simulated object navigation versus 45.00 for the strongest baseline (Gemini 3.0) and 31.67 for SPOC (31.37 in the appendix table), with zero VLM tokens; SPL 39.07 slightly above Gemini's 37.81 while SEL is slightly below. In the real world it gets 55.56 SR versus 23.08 for Gemini 3.0. It also beats DFoT/NWM/GEN3C on 2D metrics and DFoT-VGGT on all 3D-CORE tasks.
limitations: Assumes a static world; no dynamic scenes
Semantic quality is bounded by CLIP-style alignment; adding a VLM for semantics improves navigation (SR 45.83→49.58)
Small evaluation scale (120 sim episodes, few real trials), wide confidence intervals, and 3D-CORE is evaluated against only one constructed baseline
